narrative.intro: Mistral obligated $213M in FY2026 to date across 9 awards, with an average award size of $23.7M and obligations up 384.3% year over year. Mistral’s fiscal-year obligations rose from $44M in FY25 to $213M in FY26. The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer, providing $213M in obligations. Other named buyers include the Department of Justice with $7.4K. Industry concentration centers on Other Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $191M and Aircraft Manufacturing at $22.5M. Historical activity shows minimal earlier-year obligations: $224K in FY21, $39.4K in FY22, $0 in FY23, and $727K in FY24. The note clarifies that figures labeled obligations are contract obligations while award-value figures in largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables are total contract values, and that current-year totals are fiscal year to date. This profile shows a rapid spending increase in FY26 concentrated in defense-related manufacturing markets and with a small count of high-value awards driving the total obligations.

sections.heading: Who are Mistral’s top federal customers?
sections.body: The Department of Defense obligated $213M to Mistral in FY2026 to date. The Department of Justice obligated $7.4K. Those two agencies are the only buyers listed for FY2026 to date, so FY2026 activity is highly concentrated with one dominant customer.

sections.heading: What products and markets drive Mistral’s obligations?
sections.body: Other Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing accounted for $191M in obligations. Aircraft Manufacturing accounted for $22.5M, while smaller markets include Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment Repair and Maintenance at $15.1K and Irradiation Apparatus Manufacturing at $7.4K. The FY2026 total reflects a shift toward defense-related manufacturing markets.

faq.q: How much does Mistral make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Mistral has obligated $213M in federal contracts in FY2026 to date. Mistral received those obligations across 9 awards, with an average award size of $23.7M and obligations up 384.3% year over year. Historical annual obligations were $44M in FY25, $727K in FY24, $0 in FY23, $39.4K in FY22, and $224K in FY21.

The Department of Defense is Mistral’s primary buyer, obligating $213M in FY2026 to date. The Department of Justice is also listed, obligating $7.4K. No other agencies are named in the top buyers list for FY2026 to date.

faq.q: What does Mistral sell to the government?
faq.a: Mistral sells products in defense-related manufacturing markets. Other Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing drove $191M in obligations and Aircraft Manufacturing drove $22.5M. Smaller obligations are in Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment Repair and Maintenance at $15.1K and Irradiation Apparatus Manufacturing at $7.4K.
